rows.answer: The team settled on an LCD touch screen operated by fingers with a side scroll wheel, and no physical buttons. The final remote included an LCD touch screen, a normal scroll wheel, a physical on/off button, chargeable batteries with a docking station, and functions for volume, channel, digits, mute, teletext menu, and battery indicator.
rows.gold: By the third meeting they had decided on no buttons, only an LCD screen (Speaker B, the User Interface Designer, designed it). The final remote had the LCD screen plus a microphone for speech recognition.

rows.answer: In their third meeting (meeting c), the team settled on a rubber case with a spongy feel after debating soft/spongy rubber versus hard rubber. Speaker C and Speaker D favored soft rubber that feels spongy and can be pressed in, while Speaker B objected that the rubber should not be mouldable and proposed hard rubber as better because it bounces back when dropped. Speaker A decided the remote needs a spongy feel. In their final meeting (meeting d), Speaker D described the settled material as "spongy... that's rubber."
rows.gold: In the third meeting they settled on rubber (younger people like soft, spongy materials, older people like wood) and debated soft rubber (Speakers C and D) against hard rubber (Speaker B: it bounces back when dropped). In the final meeting it was described as hard rubber, not very spongy, with the idea of printing a wood-like look on it.

rows.answer: Speaker A, Speaker B, and Speaker D all pushed back on adding an LCD display. Speaker B objected that an LCD would exceed the 12.50 Euro cost limit; Speaker A objected that it would be redundant with the base station and TV, and that it did not fit the sturdy plastic-and-rubber design image or the team’s simplicity philosophy; Speaker D objected that the team did not know what to show on the display and that an LCD would be fragile. The final design did not include an LCD display, as Speaker A decided to skip it.
rows.gold: Speaker A objected that an LCD did not fit the sturdy, throwable plastic-and-soft-rubber design they were after (Speaker D agreed it is fragile), while Speaker B argued it was up to the market if it was trendy. The final design had no LCD.
